cards.text: Jehu, Israel's new king, gathers all the people for a big announcement. Then he says it: "Ahab served Baal a little, but Jehu will serve him a lot." That's like the new manager saying, "The last guy took a lot of days off? Oh, watch me take MORE."

cards.question: Jehu orders every prophet, servant and priest of Baal summoned, with nobody missing. What does he say he has planned for Baal?
And for any of Baal's prophets, servants or priests who don't show up, what does Jehu say will happen?
Jehu is truly planning to serve Baal.

cards.text: Jehu is acting deceptively so he can destroy the servants of Baal, and the man is COMMITTED. He orders a solemn assembly for Baal, and the word goes out through all of Israel.

cards.question: A few of Baal's servants decide to skip Jehu's assembly for Baal.

cards.text: Every last one of them shows up, and the temple of Baal is filled from end to end, packed tighter than a cookie box on Christmas Eve. Then Jehu turns to the keeper of the wardrobe with an order.

cards.question: Jehu tells the keeper of the wardrobe to bring out ___ for all the servants of Baal.

cards.text: Everybody's dressed for the occasion. Then Jehu walks in with Jehonadab son of Rechab, the man Jehu took along in his chariot (2 Kings 10:16), and he gives Baal's servants one more instruction.

cards.question: Jehu tells Baal's servants to look around and make sure nobody from one group is in the temple with them. Which group?

cards.text: Inside, they go in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Outside, Jehu has quietly posted guards around the building.

cards.question: Jehu stations ___ men outside the temple of Baal.
Jehu warns his guards that whoever lets even one of the men escape will forfeit his own life for theirs.

cards.text: When the burnt offering is finished, Jehu gives the order to the guards and officers: go in and kill them, and don't let anyone out.

cards.question: The guards and officers strike down Baal's servants and throw the bodies out. Where do they go next?

answers.text: Into the inner room of Baal's temple
Up to the king's palace in Samaria
Out to the city gate of Jezreel

cards.text: Out of that inner room, they haul the sacred pillar of the temple of Baal.

cards.question: What do Jehu's men do with the sacred pillar from Baal's temple?

cards.text: They demolish the sacred pillar of Baal, tear down his temple and turn it into a latrine, which it is to this day. From temple to latrine is the BIGGEST demotion I've ever heard of, friend, and I went from the kitchen counter to the junk drawer.

cards.question: With his servants gone and his temple torn down, Jehu wipes ___ out of Israel.

cards.text: But Jehu hangs on to the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat, Israel's first king after the kingdom split (1 Kings 12:20), caused Israel to commit. It's like scrubbing the whole kitchen spotless and leaving one dirty pan sitting right there in the sink.

cards.question: Jeroboam's sins that Jehu doesn't turn away from are the worship of the golden calves at ___ and ___.

cards.text: Nevertheless, the LORD speaks to Jehu. Jehu has done well carrying out what is right in the LORD's sight, and he's done to the house of Ahab all that was in the LORD's heart.

cards.question: Because Jehu carried out what was right against the house of Ahab, what does the LORD promise him?

answers.text: Four generations of his sons on Israel's throne
Victory over every enemy of Israel
A long reign of one hundred years

cards.question: Jehu is careful to follow the instruction of the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart.

cards.text: In those days, the LORD begins to reduce the size of Israel. Someone starts defeating the Israelites all through their territory.

cards.question: Who defeats the Israelites throughout their territory in Jehu's day?
Hazael's victories stretch from the Jordan eastward through all the land of Gilead.

cards.text: The rest of Jehu's acts, his accomplishments and his might are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel. Then Jehu rests with his fathers and is buried in Samaria.

cards.question: After Jehu is buried in Samaria, who reigns in his place?
Jehu reigns over Israel in Samaria for ___ years.

findings.problem: This true or false card asks whether Jehu is truly planning to serve Baal, but nothing before it hints that he is deceiving anyone. Card 1 plays his announcement straight, and cards 2 and 3 only add the summons and the threat. The baker is left with a coin flip or outside knowledge for the main twist of the passage. The story card before it needs to give enough context for a reasoned pick.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: Most of the stop's choice cards are discovery questions that can't be reasoned out from earlier cards: card 6 (Bethel and Dan), card 8 (four generations), card 11 (Hazael), card 12 (the Jordan and Gilead), card 14 (Jehoahaz) and card 15 (twenty-eight years). Only cards 2, 4 and 9 are informed guesses, so discovery questions outnumber informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Verse 33 is a list of land boundaries (the Jordan, Gilead, Gad, Reuben, Manasseh, Aroer, the Arnon, Bashan). It should be summed up on a story card, not asked on a choice card. As a true or false card it is also a coin flip.

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: The question says "his servants" and "his temple" without naming whose. That "his" points back to earlier cards. Because the blank is the name itself, the question also gives no real context. It should name who and what directly and ask something the baker has to work out.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The card says the pillar is hauled "Out of that inner room." Verse 26 says only that they brought out the sacred pillar of the temple of Baal. It never says the pillar was in the inner room. Verse 25 ends with them going into the inner room, but the text doesn't connect the two.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question says "Because Jehu carried out what was right against the house of Ahab." That merges verse 30's two reasons into one: doing what is right in the LORD's sight, and doing to the house of Ahab all that was in His heart. Merging them connects the two in a way the text doesn't.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The right answer "Burn it" is two words. The wrong answers, "Carry it to Jezreel" and "Bury it outside the city," are noticeably longer, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "three hundred" is two words. The right answer "eighty" and the other wrong answer "twenty" are one word each, so the answers aren't the same length.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card is one flat sentence of retelling with no Papa Dorin voice. Other story cards read the same way: stop 1 cards 11 and 14, and stop 2 cards 7, 10 and 13.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Across the walkthrough, only a few cards carry real humor: stop 1 cards 1 and 7, and stop 2 cards 3 and 5. Most story cards read like plain narration, not laugh-out-loud Papa Dorin.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The right answer is "Hazael king of Aram." The passage says only "Hazael." "King of Aram" comes from outside the passage (2 Kings 8:13-15). The card cites only 2 Kings 10:32, and the answer can't hold a reference.
findings.question: When a choice card's right answer uses a fact from outside the passage, like identifying a new person, does the card's verses field need to cite that outside reference? Or should the outside fact go on a story card instead?
